chapter.title: Estimation, Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Procedures

sections.title: Neyman's confidence constructions and repeated-sampling coverage

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C001 (partial): Not met: 'preserve the identified source variants'. The held source's own sum system S2 is neither reproduced nor recorded. In Neyman 1937, journal p. 357 eqs (46)-(48) and p. 358 eqs (50)-(51), eq. (47) gives P = 1-(Delta/theta)^2, so Delta = theta(1-alpha)^(1/2). The band is theta(1-(1-alpha)^(1/2)) <= x1+x2 <= theta(1+(1-alpha)^(1/2)) and the limits are S/(1+(1-alpha)^(1/2)) and S/(1-(1-alpha)^(1/2)). Under the 'Example I' heading, body lines 30, 39 and 43 of handbook/parts/p15/neyman-confidence-constructions.tex instead display a different band, qt <= S <= (2-q)t, with half-width (1-q)t and I2=[S/(2-q),S/q]. They give no note of the change. The two coincide only at alpha=3/4; for every other alpha the displayed 'three systems' are not the source's. This is an unrecorded substitution that the text implicitly attributes to the source. The handbook mathematics itself is correct.

ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C002 (partial): Not met: 'preserve the identified source variants'. The source computes the coverage of its sum system in eq. (47), p. 357: P{E in A2(theta)|theta} = 1-(Delta/theta)^2, hence Delta = theta(1-alpha)^(1/2). Its claim (53), p. 358, says the coverage frequency is alpha for every 0<alpha<1. The handbook neither reproduces nor records either. Annex lines 29-36 derive 1-(1-Delta/theta)^2 and contradict eq. (47) silently. The treatment omits that the source's printed band has coverage 1-(1-(1-alpha)^(1/2))^2, which equals alpha only at alpha=3/4 and is about 0.397 at alpha=0.95. The rest of the component is present in complete form: the S1 empty-section failure with probability beta, the sum density, and the n-sample maximum law and interval.

ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C003 (partial): Not met: 'preserve the identified source variants', in a component titled 'The source's length and repeated-experiment comparisons'. (i) The source's eq. (52), p. 358, gives delta2 = 2(x1+x2)(1-alpha)^(1/2)/alpha. Without any record, the handbook replaces it with D2 = 2(1-q)S/(q(2-q)) at body line 81 and E D2 = 2(1-q)theta/(q(2-q)) at line 88; they agree only at alpha=3/4. (ii) The source's eq. (69), p. 362, states the strict bound (3/8)delta2 < delta3. This bound fails at the source's own sample A = (1,1), where the ratio is exactly 3/8. Body lines 83-85 and 95 silently replace it with a closed bound plus an equality case and do not record the source's statement. The alpha=3/4 sample intervals, the 400-trial schedule, the 0.69/0.81 limits and the binomial law are preserved and proved.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-student-inference-C010 (partial): Two elements of the success condition are missing for one sentence of this entry. (1) 'Construction or argument' and 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.student.one.sided.optimal): handbook/parts/p15/student-inference.tex l.286-288 says the one-sided rejection cones 'impose no requirement that every coordinate have the same sign'. The declared proof (handbook/annex/p15/student-inference.tex l.439-500) never argues this. (2) 'Preserve the identified source variants': at the cited locator, the held NP1933 PDF p.32 (journal p.319) says the best critical cones lie in the quadrant of positive x's for a_t>a_0, and of negative x's for a_t<a_0. The entry contradicts this and does not state the regime in which each holds. The cap {Z_m>c_+} lies inside the same-sign orthant of x-m1 exactly when t_{nu,alpha}>=nu. For n=2, alpha=3/4, phi_m^+ rejects iff min x_i>m; this matches the entry's own worked interval [1,infinity) for the sample (1,3) at l.403-405. For n=3, alpha=0.95, t_{2,0.95}~2.92>=2, which matches NP's n=3 picture. So the remark needs an argument that carries this qualification, or it should be removed, and the source's quadrant description needs to be kept with its regime. Every other element of C010 is present: body l.272-285 and 288-292, annex l.441-498.
